●Why This Exists, What It Does & What It Doesn’t Do
Why This Exists (And Why Beating ADP Is Possible)
Fantasy leagues are actually well projected in general—consensus ADP gets most players roughly right, and throwing it away to guess from scratch loses badly. The edge comes from repeatable human error and biases on a small group of players: overpaying for rookie hype, aging/injury-prone names, and flashy scoring while overlooking durable, efficient multi-category starters. Avoiding a few landmines and hitting a few undervalued targets is what builds league-winning teams.
What This Board Does
Publishes balanced, ADP-based pre-draft 9-Cat projections (Z-scores across PTS, REB, AST, STL, BLK, 3PM, volume-weighted FG%/FT%, and 0.75× TO) that power both Roto and H2H. Optional Punt chips let punters re-rank as a reference lens alongside ADP—your draft-day tactics are up to you.
What It Doesn’t Do
It does not consider mid-season moves, waiver streaming, trades, mid-season injuries, or coaching/rotation changes after Opening Night, and it is not an explicit draft script. This is purely a way to get an edge on draft day—the rest of the season is up to the manager.
How to Read Z-Scores & Replay
Each category is shown in standard deviations (Z-score) vs. the Top-180 pool: green (+1.0+) is an elite strength, red (-1.0) is a drag. Green Edge marks players projected ahead of ADP; scrub the slider below to replay any season game by game.
